frames.narration: The login code builds its query by pasting the typed name into a string. A normal user types alice.
The attacker types a name that contains a quote and extra logic: ' OR '1'='1.
Pasted into the string, the query becomes WHERE name = '' OR '1'='1'. The database cannot tell which part was meant to be data, so the condition is always true and it returns every user.
The fix: send the query and the value separately. The query has a placeholder, and the value travels as data.
The database looks for a user whose name is literally the odd text ' OR '1'='1. There is none, so it returns nothing. The attack input was only ever data.
Same shape in a web page: a review contains a script tag. If the page inserts it as HTML, every visitor's browser runs it with their session. Encoding output turns it into harmless visible text.
